You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

install anything! For your convenience, prebuilt binaries for Linux, OSX and Windows are provided that should run without any dependencies. **Additionally, there is a web version available.**

It's compatible with FreeBSD, Linux, macOS, Windows, and most modern web browsers that support WebAssembly.

**On FreeBSD**: You can install via package manager:

    pkg install genact
    genact

**On Linux**: Download `genact-linux` from the releases page and run:

    chmod +x genact-linux
    ./genact-linux

**On macOS**: Download `genact-osx` from the releases page and run:

    chmod +x genact-osx
    ./genact-osx

A homebrew package is also available:

    brew install genact

On macOS, you can also install via MacPorts:

    sudo port install genact

**On Windows**: Download `genact-win.exe` from the releases page and double click it.

It is also available on Scoop:

    scoop install genact

## Running

To see a list of all available options, you can run:

    ./genact -h

or (on Docker):

    docker run -it --rm svenstaro/genact -h

# genact - a nonsense activity generator

**Pretend to be busy or waiting for your computer when you should actually be doing real work!** Impress people with your insane multitasking skills. Just open a few instances of `genact` and watch the show. `genact` has multiple scenes that pretend to be doing something exciting or useful when in reality nothing is happening at all.

![](gifs/cc.gif)
![](gifs/memdump.gif)
![](gifs/cargo.gif)

## Installation

You don't have to install anything! For your convenience, prebuilt binaries for Linux, OSX and Windows are provided that should run without any dependencies. **Additionally, there is a web version available.**

It's compatible with FreeBSD, Linux, macOS, Windows, and most modern web browsers that support WebAssembly.

**On FreeBSD**: You can install via package manager:

    pkg install genact
    genact

**On Linux**: Download `genact-linux` from the releases page and run:

    chmod +x genact-linux
    ./genact-linux

**On macOS**: Download `genact-osx` from the releases page and run:

    chmod +x genact-osx
    ./genact-osx

A homebrew package is also available:

    brew install genact

On macOS, you can also install via MacPorts:

    sudo port install genact

**On Windows**: Download `genact-win.exe` from the releases page and double click it.

It is also available on Scoop:

    scoop install genact

## Running

To see a list of all available options, you can run:

    ./genact -h

or (on Docker):

    docker run -it --rm svenstaro/genact -h

### Usage

    A nonsense activity generator

    Usage: genact [OPTIONS]

    Options:
      -l, --list-modules                               List available modules
      -m, --modules <MODULES>                          Run only these modules [possible values: ansible, bootlog, botnet, bruteforce, cargo, cc, composer,
                                                       cryptomining, docker_build, docker_image_rm, download, julia, kernel_compile, memdump, mkinitcpio,
                                                       rkhunter, simcity, terraform, uv, weblog, wpt]
      -s, --speed-factor <SPEED_FACTOR>                Global speed factor [default: 1]
      -i, --instant-print-lines <INSTANT_PRINT_LINES>  Instantly print this many lines [default: 0]
          --exit-after-time <EXIT_AFTER_TIME>          Exit after running for this long (format example: 2h10min)
          --exit-after-modules <EXIT_AFTER_MODULES>    Exit after running this many modules
          --print-completions <shell>                  Generate completion file for a shell [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh]
          --print-manpage                              Generate man page
      -h, --help                                       Print help
      -V, --version                                    Print version

### Web usage

You can also provide a `?speed-factor` parameter to adjust the speed.

import subprocess, time, os, signal, sys

def run_module(mod, timeout=4):
    print(f"\n===== MODULE {mod} =====")
    try:
        # Use exit-after-modules 1 and timeout
        p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable","-m",mod,"--exit-after-modules","1"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, bufsize=1)
        try:
            out, err = p.communicate(timeout=timeout)
            print(f"EXIT {p.returncode} OUT len {len(out)} ERR len {len(err)}")
            print("OUT HEAD:", repr(out[:4000]))
            if len(out)>4000:
                print("OUT TAIL:", repr(out[-2000:]))
            print("ERR:", repr(err[:2000]))
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            p.kill()
            out, err = p.communicate()
            print(f"TIMEOUT KILLED OUT len {len(out)}")
            print("OUT HEAD:", repr(out[:5000]))
            if len(out)>5000:
                print("OUT TAIL:", repr(out[-2000:]))
            print("ERR:", repr(err[:2000]))
    except Exception as e:
        print(e)

for mod in ["ansible","bootlog","botnet"]:
    run_module(mod, timeout=6)

def run_tty(mod, duration=3):
    # Use script to provide tty
    # script -qec "cmd" /dev/null
    cmd = ["script","-qec", f"./executable -m {mod} --exit-after-modules 1", "/dev/null"]
    p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)

        print(f"{mod} exit={p.returncode} outlen={len(out)} errlen={len(err)}")
        print("OUT:", repr(out[:3000]))
        print("ERR:", repr(err[:1000]))
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        p.kill()
        out,err = p.communicate()
        print(f"{mod} TIMEOUT outlen={len(out)}")
        print("OUT HEAD:", repr(out[:3000]))
        print("OUT TAIL:", repr(out[-2000:]) if len(out)>3000 else "")
        print("ERR:", repr(err[:1000]))

for mod in ["ansible","download"]:
    run_tty(mod, duration=4)

using namespace System.Management.Automation.Language

Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native -CommandName 'genact' -ScriptBlock {
    param($wordToComplete, $commandAst, $cursorPosition)

    $commandElements = $commandAst.CommandElements
    $command = @(
        'genact'
        for ($i = 1; $i -lt $commandElements.Count; $i++) {
            $element = $commandElements[$i]
            if ($element -isnot [StringConstantExpressionAst] -or
                $element.StringConstantType -ne [StringConstantType]::BareWord -or
                $element.Value.StartsWith('-') -or
                $element.Value -eq $wordToComplete) {
                break
        }
        $element.Value
    }) -join ';'

    $completions = @(switch ($command) {
        'genact' {

{"command": "python3 <<'PY'
import subprocess, time, os

def cap(mod, exit_time="800ms", outer=12):
    # use tmux + file to get tty for download/ansible, but also for others
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-s","test","-x","200","-y","50"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    try: os.remove("/tmp/out.txt")
    except: pass
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","test", f"timeout {outer} ./executable -m {mod} --exit-after-time {exit_time} > /tmp/out.txt 2>&1; echo DONE:$?", "Enter"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(outer+1)
    try:
        with open("/tmp/out.txt","rb") as f:
            data=f.read()
        txt=data.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
        print(f"=== {mod} len {len(data)} ===")
        print(txt[:3000])
        print("---TAIL---")
        print(txt[-1000:])
        print()
    except Exception as e:
        print(e)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"], capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.2)

for mod in ["download","ansible","julia","rkhunter","uv","wpt"]:
    cap(mod, exit_time="800ms", outer=8)
PY
"}

**Pretend to be busy or waiting for your computer when you should actually be doing real work!** Impress people with your insane multitasking skills. Just open a few instances of `genact` and watch the show. `genact` has multiple scenes that pretend to be doing something exciting or useful when in reality nothing is happening at all.

You don't have to install anything! For your convenience, prebuilt binaries for Linux, OSX and Windows are provided that should run without any dependencies. **Additionally, there is a web version available.**

It's compatible with FreeBSD, Linux, macOS, Windows, and most modern web browsers that support WebAssembly.

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
use rand::seq::SliceRandom;

static INTERRUPTED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

fn setup_signal_handler() {
    unsafe {
        // Use signal-hook for SIGINT/SIGTERM? For simplicity use libc signal handler that sets flag
        // We'll use signal-hook crate if available, else fallback to libc
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            extern "C" fn handler(_: libc::c_int) {
                INTERRUPTED.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
            }
            libc::signal(libc::SIGINT, handler as usize);
            libc::signal(libc::SIGTERM, handler as usize);
        }
    }
}

pub struct Context {
    pub speed: f64,
    pub instant_left: u32,
    pub start: Instant,
    pub exit_after: Option<Duration>,
}

impl Context {
    pub fn new(speed: f64, instant: u32, exit_after: Option<Duration>) -> Self {
        Self {
            speed,
            instant_left: instant,
            start: Instant::now(),
            exit_after,
        }
    }
    pub fn should_exit(&self) -> bool {
        if INTERRUPTED.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            return true;
        }
        if let Some(d) = self.exit_after {
            if self.start.elapsed() >= d {
                return true;
            }
        }
        false
    }
    pub fn sleep(&mut self, base_millis: u64) {
        if self.instant_left > 0 {
            self.instant_left -= 1;
            return;
        }
        if base_millis == 0 {
            return;
        }
        let adjusted = (base_millis as f64 / self.speed) as u64;
        // add some jitter? Use fixed
        if adjusted == 0 {
            // tiny sleep to allow signal checking? No, return immediately but check exit?
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_micros(500));
            return;
        }
        // Sleep in small chunks to be responsive to exit time/signal (overshoot like original is okay, but we want responsive)
        // Original overshoots by up to 1-2s, but we will be more responsive (check every 10ms)
        let mut remaining = adjusted;
        while remaining > 0 {
            if self.should_exit() {
                break;
            }
            let chunk = std::cmp::min(remaining, 10);
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(chunk));
            remaining -= chunk;
        }
    }
    pub fn print(&mut self, s: &str, base_millis: u64) -> bool {
        // returns false if should exit after (caller should abort module)
        if self.should_exit() {
            return false;
        }
        {
            use std::io::Write;
            let mut out = std::io::stdout().lock();
            let _ = out.write_all(s.as_bytes());
            let _ = out.write_all(b"\r\n");
            let _ = out.flush();
        }
        self.sleep(base_millis);
        !self.should_exit()
    }
    pub fn print_no_sleep(&mut self, s: &str) {
        use std::io::Write;
        let mut out = std::io::stdout().lock();
        let _ = out.write_all(s.as_bytes());
        let _ = out.write_all(b"\r\n");
        let _ = out.flush();
    }
}

        }
        {

            let mut out = std::io::stdout().lock();
            let _ = out.write_all(s.as_bytes());
            let _ = out.write_all(b"\r\n");
            let _ = out.flush();
        }
        self.sleep(base_millis);
        !self.should_exit()
    }
    pub fn print_raw(&mut self, s: &str) {
        use std::io::Write;
        let mut out = std::io::stdout().lock();
        let _ = out.write_all(s.as_bytes());
        let _ = out.flush();
    }
}

pub fn interrupted() -> bool {
    INTERRUPTED.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
}

pub fn run(selected: Vec<String>, speed: f64, instant: u32, exit_after_time: Option<Duration>, exit_after_modules: Option<u32>) {
    setup_signal_handler();
    let all_modules = vec![
        "ansible",
        "bootlog",
        "botnet",
        "bruteforce",
        "cargo",
        "cc",
        "composer",
        "cryptomining",
        "docker_build",
        "docker_image_rm",
        "download",
        "julia",
        "kernel_compile",
        "memdump",
        "mkinitcpio",
        "rkhunter",
        "simcity",
        "terraform",
        "uv",
        "weblog",
        "wpt",
    ];
    let pool: Vec<String> = if selected.is_empty() {
        all_modules.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect()
    } else {
        selected
    };

    let start = Instant::now();
    let mut modules_done: u32 = 0;
    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
    let mut instant_left = instant;

    loop {
        if let Some(d) = exit_after_time {
            if start.elapsed() >= d {
                break;
            }
        }
        if let Some(limit) = exit_after_modules {
            if modules_done >= limit {
                break;
            }
        }
        if interrupted() {
            break;
        }
        let choice = pool.choose(&mut rng).unwrap().clone();
        let mut ctx = Context {
            speed,
            instant_left,
            start,
            exit_after: exit_after_time,
        };
        let _completed = crate::modules::run_module(&choice, &mut ctx);
        instant_left = ctx.instant_left;
        if ctx.should_exit() || interrupted() {
            break;
        } else {
            modules_done += 1;
            continue;
        }
    }

    println!("Saving work to disk...");
}

fn run_simcity(ctx: &mut Context) -> bool {
    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
    let tasks = ["Dicing Models...","Fixing Election Outcome Matrix...","Bureacritizing Bureaucracies...","Integrating Curves...","Weathering Buildings...","Zoning Districts...","Simulating Traffic...","Calibrating Taxes...","Deploying Services..."];
    // simcity runs tasks sequentially, each with spinner for a while, then OK or ABORTED, then ALL DONE
    for _ in 0..3 {
        let task = tasks.choose(&mut rng).unwrap();
        let spinner = ['/','-','\\','|'];
        for i in 0..16 {
            let line = format!("[ ] {} {}", task, spinner[i % 4]);
            {
                use std::io::Write;
                let mut out = std::io::stdout().lock();
                let _ = out.write_all(line.as_bytes());
                let _ = out.write_all(b"\r\n");
                let _ = out.flush();
            }
            if ctx.instant_left > 0 { ctx.instant_left -= 1; } else { ctx.sleep(80); }
            if ctx.should_exit() { return false; }
        }
        // finish: OK or ABORTED?
        let ok = rng.gen_bool(0.7);
        if ok {
            let line = format!("[o] \x1b[37m{} OK\x1b[0m", task);
            if !ctx.print(&line, 100) { return false; }
        } else {
            let line = format!("[o] \x1b[31m{} ABORTED\x1b[0m", task);
            // Original: "[o] Fixing... ABORTED" with red? Actually sample: "[o] Fixing... ABORTED" in red. Good.
            if !ctx.print(&line, 100) { return false; }
            // After ABORTED, print ALL DONE and return? Sample simcity with ABORTED then ALL DONE. Good.
            if !ctx.print("ALL DONE", 100) { return false; }
            return true;
        }
    }
    if !ctx.print("ALL DONE", 100) { return false; }
    true
}

fn run_terraform(ctx: &mut Context) -> bool {
    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
    if !ctx.print("Acquiring state lock. This may take a few moments...", 300) { return false; }
    let resources = ["aws_api_gateway_client_certificate","aws_ec2_tag","aws_grafana_workspace","aws_networkmanager_connect_attachment","aws_servicecatalog_product","aws_appsync_domain_name_api_association","aws_s3control_bucket","google_storage_bucket_acl","google_compute_network_attachment","aws_securityhub_action_target","aws_infinidash","aws_workspaces_ip_group","aws_shield_protection_health_check_association","aws_internet_gateway_attachment","aws_media_convert_queue","aws_cloudformation_type","aws_ivs_playback_key_pair","aws_dynamodb_tag","aws_ecr_registry_scanning_configuration","aws_redshiftserverless_namespace","aws_dx_connection_confirmation","aws_datasync_location_efs","aws_apprunner_auto_scaling_configuration_version","aws_subnet","aws_verifiedaccess_group","aws_s3_bucket_logging","aws_resourceexplorer2_view","aws_timestreamwrite_table","aws_cloudtrail","aws_waf_rate_based_rule","aws_connect_bot_association","aws_opensearch_domain_saml_options","aws_prometheus_alert_manager_definition","aws_fms_policy","aws_cognito_user_in_group","aws_datasync_location_smb","aws_opsworks_rds_db_instance","aws_storagegateway_smb_file_share","aws_codecommit_trigger","aws_ssm_association","google_dataform_repository_release_config","google_compute_region_instance_template","google_bigquery_analytics_hub_listing","google_logging_organization_settings","google_compute_router_peer"];
    let actions = ["Creating...","Modifying... [id=","Refreshing state... [id=","Creation complete after ","Modifications complete after ","Destruction complete after ","Still creating... [","Still modifying... [id=","Destroying... [id="];
    // Terraform prints many lines, then Apply complete
    for _ in 0..30 {
        let res = resources.choose(&mut rng).unwrap();
        let suffix = format!("{}.{}", rand_word(&mut rng), rand_word(&mut rng));
        // Actually resource format: aws_... .name: action
        let act = actions.choose(&mut rng).unwrap();
        let line = if act.contains("complete after") {
            let secs = rng.gen_range(0..7);
            format!("\x1b[1m{}.{}: {} {}s [id={}]\x1b[0m", res, suffix.trim_matches(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric()), act, secs, suffix)
        } else if act.contains("Still") {
            let secs = rng.gen_range(0..7);
            if act.contains("creating") {
                format!("\x1b[1m{}.{}: {} {}s elapsed]\x1b[0m", res, suffix, act, secs)
            } else {
                format!("\x1b[1m{}.{}: {} {}, {}s elapsed]\x1b[0m", res, suffix, act, suffix, secs)
            }
        } else if act.contains("[id=") {
            format!("\x1b[1m{}.{}: {} {}]\x1b[0m", res, suffix, act, suffix)
        } else {
            format!("\x1b[1m{}.{}: {}\x1b[0m", res, suffix, act)
        };
        if !ctx.print(&line, 180) { return false; }
    }
    if !ctx.print("", 100) { return false; }
    let added = rng.gen_range(0..3);
    let changed = rng.gen_range(0..5);
    let destroyed = rng.gen_range(0..2);
    if !ctx.print(&format!("Apply complete! Resources: {} added, {} changed, {} destroyed.", added, changed, destroyed), 200) { return false; }
    true
}

fn run_uv(ctx: &mut Context) -> bool {
    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
